title: Form 6 — New Elector Registration
summary: Form 6 is used only for first-time registration as an elector, including when a first registration is triggered by moving to a new place of ordinary residence. Since the 2022 amendment it no longer covers corrections or shifting of an existing entry — that is Form 8.
body:
Use Form 6 if you are registering as a voter for the first time. This includes: turning 18 and enrolling for the first time; moving to a new place and choosing to register there for the first time (rather than transferring an existing entry, which uses Form 8); or a student choosing to register at a hostel/mess address under the ordinary-residence provision.

Form 6 is not used for corrections to an existing entry, replacement of a lost/damaged EPIC, or shifting an existing registration — those are handled through Form 8. Objecting to or seeking deletion of someone else's entry (e.g., after death, or a duplicate/ineligible entry) uses Form 7.

General document categories typically requested (confirm current list on the official portal, as requirements can be updated by ECI/state CEOs): proof of age, proof of ordinary residence, a recent passport-style photograph, and (for students registering at a hostel/mess) a bonafide certificate from the head of the institution.

Apply online via the official ECI portal, or through the Voter Helpline App, or in person via your Booth Level Officer (BLO) / Electoral Registration Officer (ERO).

sources.title: Forms for Registration in Electoral Roll

caution: Requirements and the exact document list can change by ECI notification. Always confirm the current requirements on voters.eci.gov.in before applying.
